subject: BFCL task wall timeout as a task-local harness failure with engine session release

incident.observed: the last recorded step (turn-1/step-3) was ok; the server journals stopped at 11:31 while the next generation was in flight, and run_c1's worker.wait raised subprocess.TimeoutExpired at 10796 s; no final.json was written (the controller was killed mid-request); the TimeoutExpired escaped benchmarks.paper.c1's RuntimeError/CalledProcessError fallback and the remaining 43 tasks of the shard were not run

change.run_c1: run_task raises TaskWallTimeout (a RuntimeError) when the official BFCL worker outlives the task limit; after stopping the worker and controller it calls release_engine_session, which aborts the in-flight engine request with the transport's lost-response call (/abort_request, wait_for_completion, close_session) or closes the idle session, and records a receipt without raising
change.benchmarks.paper.c1: run_closed_loop scores a TaskWallTimeout 0 as status harness_failure, kind task_timeout (with timeout, elapsed and the engine cleanup receipt) and continues; the cell summary counts it under n_harness_failures

unchanged: Tasks that finish within the limit run the same code and produce the same receipts.
Controller readiness timeouts, worker non-zero exits and every other failure keep their previous handling.
tau2, ToolSandbox, ACEBench and AppWorld runners are not changed; their own official-harness timeouts still end the cell.

tests.file: benchmarks/paper/test_c1_task_timeout.py (2 new; both fail on 1afe5ff, the first with the live subprocess.TimeoutExpired)
tests.integration: the real run_c1.run_task with a controller blocked on an in-flight generation, a sleeping worker and a stand-in engine: the timed-out task is scored 0 as harness_failure/task_timeout, the engine receives one /abort_request for the in-flight rid and session, and the next task completes
tests.suites: benchmarks, runtime memory_runtime and delivery suites have the same failure sets as 1afe5ff

open: Scoring a timed-out task 0 is hardware dependent (the off arms finish task 107 in time on the same GPU type). The receipt marks it as a harness failure, not a model decision; whether such tasks are rerun with a larger limit or on faster GPUs, or reported as failures, is an evaluation decision.

Aborting a request during chunked prefill is not honoured by engine 89c3895d7 (the abort fix 36e969135 is on a separate branch). The receipt then reports status failed, and the engine finishes the orphaned request and later reaps the session.
